43127-an-enchanted-garden-fairy-stories.title: An Enchanted Garden Fairy Stories
43127-an-enchanted-garden-fairy-stories.creator: Mrs Molesworth
43127-an-enchanted-garden-fairy-stories.description: A book by Mrs Molesworth. This was their trouble. They could not get any one to tell them any more stories! They had read all their books through, over and over again, and besides, books aren't _quite_ as nice as "told" stories. At least not when they have to be shared by two. Rafe and Alix had tried several plans--reading aloud did not answer _very_ well, and looking over the pages was worse.

65123-gold-hunting-in-alaska.title: Gold Hunting In Alaska
65123-gold-hunting-in-alaska.creator: Unknown
65123-gold-hunting-in-alaska.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. s continually going to Alaska as to their responsibility to each other and to the natives of the "frozen North." It may give "the folks at home" some intimation as to possible "good times" under trying circumstances. Blue fingers may not necessarily denote a blue heart.

72524-the-life-story-of-charlotte-de-la-.title: Countess of Derby
72524-the-life-story-of-charlotte-de-la-.creator: Unknown
72524-the-life-story-of-charlotte-de-la-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The Ancestry of 40  the Earls of Derby. “Sans  Changer.” A Stately Old Home. The Royal  Guest, and the Fool. The Baron’s Retainers. A Goodly “Checkrowle.” Public Troubles. The  Siege of Rochelle. “The Villain has killed  me.” National Grievances.

7623-pelham-complete.title: Pelham Complete
7623-pelham-complete.creator: Edward Bulwer Lytton
7623-pelham-complete.description: A book by Edward Bulwer Lytton. Conway had just caused two divorces; and of course, all the women in London were dying for him--judge then of the pride which Lady Frances felt at his addresses. The end of the season was unusually dull, and my mother, after having looked over her list of engagements, and ascertained that she had none remaining worth staying for, agreed to elope with her new lover.

arxiv-1809-08640.title: Comparing Video Based Shoulder Surfing with Live Simulation Thanks: This article appears in the proceedings of the 2018 Annual Computer Security Applications Conference.
arxiv-1809-08640.creator: Adam J. Aviv ∙ , Flynn Wolf ⋄ , and Ravi Kuber ⋄ ∙ United States Naval Academy ⋄ University of Maryland,Baltimore County aviv@unsa.edu {flynn.wolf,rkuber}@umbc.edu
arxiv-1809-08640.description: Abstract We analyze the claims that video recreations of shoulder surfing attacks offer a suitable alternative and a baseline, as compared to evaluation in a live setting. We recreated a subset of the factors of a prior video-simulation experiment conducted by Aviv et al.

arxiv-1904-06044.title: Unsupervised Method to Localize Masses in Mammograms Note: PhD candidate in Korea University
arxiv-1904-06044.creator: Bilal Ahmed Lodhi
arxiv-1904-06044.description: Abstract Breast cancer is one of the most common and prevalent type of cancer that mainly affects the women population. chances of effective treatment increases with early diagnosis. Mammography is considered one of the effective and proven techniques for early diagnosis of breast cancer. Tissues around masses look identical in mammogram, which makes automatic detection process a very challenging task.

arxiv-2101-05571.title: On continuous spectrum of magnetic Schrödinger operators on periodic discrete graphs
arxiv-2101-05571.creator: Evgeny Korotyaev, Natalia Saburova
arxiv-2101-05571.description: Abstract . We consider Schrödinger operators with periodic electric and magnetic potentials on periodic discrete graphs. The spectrum of such operators consists of an absolutely continuous (a.c.) part (a union of a finite number of non-degenerate bands) and a finite number of eigenvalues of infinite multiplicity. We prove the following results: 1) the a.c.

arxiv-2106-12499.title: Generative Self-training for Cross-domain Unsupervised Tagged-to-Cine MRI Synthesis
arxiv-2106-12499.creator: Xiaofeng Liu, Fangxu Xing, Maureen Stone, Jiachen Zhuo, Timothy Reese, Jerry L. Prince, Georges El Fakhri, Jonghye Woo
arxiv-2106-12499.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Xiaofeng Liu, Fangxu Xing, Maureen Stone, Jiachen Zhuo, Timothy Reese, Jerry L. Prince, Georges El Fakhri, Jonghye Woo. Self-training based unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) has shown great potential to address the problem of domain shift, when applying a trained deep learning model in a source domain to unlabeled target domains.

arxiv-2207-03554.title: G2L: A Geometric Approach for Generating Pseudo-labels that Improve Transfer Learning
arxiv-2207-03554.creator: John R. Kender, Bishwaranjan Bhattacharjee, Parijat Dube, Brian M. Belgodere
arxiv-2207-03554.description: Abstract Transfer learning is a deep-learning technique that ameliorates the problem of learning when human-annotated labels are expensive and limited. In place of such labels, it uses instead the previously trained weights from a well-chosen source model as the initial weights for the training of a base model for a new target dataset.

arxiv-2403-17364.title: A Moreau Envelope Approach for LQR Meta-Policy Estimation
arxiv-2403-17364.creator: Ashwin Aravind, Mohammad Taha Toghani, César A. Uribe
arxiv-2403-17364.description: Abstract We study the problem of policy estimation for the Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) in discrete-time linear time-invariant uncertain dynamical systems. We propose a Moreau Envelope-based surrogate LQR cost, built from a finite set of realizations of the uncertain system, to define a meta-policy efficiently adjustable to new realizations.

arxiv-2405-10316.title: Analogist: Out-of-the-box Visual In-Context Learning with Image Diffusion Model
arxiv-2405-10316.creator: Zheng Gu, Shiyuan Yang, Jing Liao, Jing Huo, Yang Gao
arxiv-2405-10316.description: Abstract . Visual In-Context Learning (ICL) has emerged as a promising research area due to its capability to accomplish various tasks with limited example pairs through analogical reasoning. However, training-based visual ICL has limitations in its ability to generalize to unseen tasks and requires the collection of a diverse task dataset.

arxiv-2408-06105.title: Text2Interaction: Establishing Safe and Preferable Human-Robot Interaction
arxiv-2408-06105.creator: Jakob Thumm, Christopher Agia, Marco Pavone, Stanford University, pavone@stanford.edu, Matthias Althoff
arxiv-2408-06105.description: Abstract Adjusting robot behavior to human preferences can require intensive human feedback, preventing quick adaptation to new users and changing circumstances. Moreover, current approaches typically treat user preferences as a reward, which requires a manual balance between task success and user satisfaction.

arxiv-2408-11736.title: Tau polarization effects in ν τ / ν ¯ τ \nu_{\tau}/\bar{\nu}_{\tau} - tungsten interactions at the LHC energies
arxiv-2408-11736.creator: Reinaldo Francener, Victor P. Gonçalves, Diego R. Gratieri
arxiv-2408-11736.description: Abstract Recent studies have demonstrated that the tau produced in charged current neutrino deeply inelastic interactions at the GeV – TeV neutrino energy range is not fully polarized. In this paper we investigate the impact of the tau polarization on the pions generated in its decay.

arxiv-2409-13955.title: On the Effectiveness of Neural Operators at Zero-Shot Weather Downscaling
arxiv-2409-13955.creator: Saumya Sinha, Brandon Benton, Patrick Emami
arxiv-2409-13955.description: Abstract Machine learning (ML) methods have shown great potential for weather downscaling. These data-driven approaches provide a more efficient alternative for producing high-resolution weather datasets and forecasts compared to physics-based numerical simulations. Neural operators, which learn solution operators for a family of partial differential equations (PDEs), have shown great success in scientific ML applications involving physics-driven datasets.

arxiv-2410-02928.title: The Outcome of Collisions between Gaseous Clumps formed by Disk Instability
arxiv-2410-02928.creator: Yoav Matzkevich, Christian Reinhardt, Thomas Meier, Joachim Stadel, Ravit Helled
arxiv-2410-02928.description: Abstract The disk instability model is a promising pathway for giant planet formation in various conditions. At the moment, population synthesis models are used to investigate the outcomes of this theory, where a key ingredient of the disk population evolution are collisions of self-gravitating clumps formed by the disk instabilities.

arxiv-2410-10552.title: Combinatorial flats and Schubert varieties of subspace arrangements
arxiv-2410-10552.creator: Colin Crowley, Connor Simpson, Botong Wang
arxiv-2410-10552.description: Abstract . The lattice of flats ℒ M \mathcal{L}_{M} of a matroid M M is combinatorially well-behaved and, when M M is realizable, admits a geometric model in the form of a “Schubert variety of hyperplane arrangement”. In contrast, the lattice of flats of a polymatroid exhibits many combinatorial pathologies and admits no similar geometric model.

arxiv-2502-10880.title: On the fluctuations of the number of atoms in the condensate
arxiv-2502-10880.creator: Maciej B. Kruk, Piotr Kulik, Malthe F. Andersen, Piotr Deuar, Mariusz Gajda, Krzysztof Pawłowski, Emilia Witkowska, Jan J. Arlt, Kazimierz Rzążewski
arxiv-2502-10880.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Maciej B. Kruk, Piotr Kulik, Malthe F. Andersen, Piotr Deuar, Mariusz Gajda, Krzysztof Pawłowski, Emilia Witkowska, Jan J. Arlt, Kazimierz Rzążewski. Bose-Einstein condensation represents a remarkable phase transition, characterized by the formation of a single quantum subsystem. As a result, the statistical properties of the condensate are highly unique. In the case of a Bose gas, while the mean number of condensed atoms is independent of the choice of statistical ensemble, the microcanonical, canonical, or grand canonical variances differ significantly among these ensembles.

arxiv-2511-20739.title: Game Theory in Cosmology
arxiv-2511-20739.creator: Oem Trivedi, Venkat Venkatasubramanian
arxiv-2511-20739.description: Abstract We present a game-theoretic statistical framework for cosmology, which we term Cosmological Teleodynamics . We recast the dark sector, cosmic acceleration, large-scale structure, and cosmic tensions as emergent consequences of nonlocal memory and intrinsically persistent organization in a self-gravitating Universe.

pmc-11310357.title: Improving the acoustic performance of flexible polyurethane foam using biochar modified by (3-aminopropyl)trimethoxysilane coupling agent
pmc-11310357.creator: Ahmed Abdelhamid Maamoun, Ramadan M. Abouomar, Tarek M. El-Basheer, Mostafa A. Azab, ElSayed G. Zaki, Shymaa M. Elsaeed, Ahmed Elkhateeb
pmc-11310357.description: This study aims to investigate the potential of integrating natural biochar (BC) derived from eggshell waste into flexible polyurethane (FPU) foam to enhance its mechanical and acoustic performance. The study explores the impact of incorporating BC at various weight ratios (0.1, 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7 wt. %) on the properties of the FPU foam.

pmc-11352269.title: Gastrointestinal Cancer Patient Derived Organoids at the Frontier of Personalized Medicine and Drug Screening
pmc-11352269.creator: Zhenjie Yang, Jun Yu, Chi Chun Wong, Bruce A Bunnell
pmc-11352269.description: Cancer is a leading cause of death worldwide. Around one-third of the total global cancer incidence and mortality are related to gastrointestinal (GI) cancers. Over the past few years, rapid developments have been made in patient-derived organoid (PDO) models for gastrointestinal cancers.

pmc-11472507.title: Don’t forget to mind the mind: a prospective cohort study over 12 months on mental health symptoms in active professional male footballers
pmc-11472507.creator: Lervasen Pillay, Dina C Janse van Rensburg, Gopika Ramkilawon, Thor Einar Andersen, Gino Kerkhoffs, Vincent Gouttebarge
pmc-11472507.description: AimsWe examined the prevalence and incidence of mental health symptoms (MHS) in active professional male footballers over a 12-month period and investigated if MHS was associated with severe injuries or surgeries.Participants and methodsFootball Players Worldwide (FIFPRO) affiliated national unions invited active professional male football players to participate in the study.

pmc-11609305.title: Assessment of clinical efficacy and safety of ICL implantation in patients with relatively shallow anterior chamber depth in early and midterm postoperative time
pmc-11609305.creator: Ting Huang, Hongyan Zhang, Ke Li
pmc-11609305.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the clinical effect and safety of Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL) implantation in myopic patients with relatively shallow anterior chamber depth (ACD).MethodsRetrospective analysis, comparative, non-interventional case series. Patients with myopia who underwent ICL implantation were included in the study and were categorized into two groups: one with a relatively shallow ACD (2.60 mm ≤ ACD ＜ 2.

pmc-11664164.title: Protocol to culture Leishmania protozoans for lipophosphoglycan extraction and purification
pmc-11664164.creator: Lisa Ulrike Teufel, Jéssica Cristina dos Santos
pmc-11664164.description: SummaryLipophosphoglycan (LPG) is a macromolecule on the surface of Leishmania spp. parasites. The biochemical structure of LPG varies throughout the parasites’ life cycle between proliferative (procyclic) and infective (metacyclic) stages, as well as between species and strains. Here, we outline a protocol for growing Leishmania parasites in vitro to harvest LPG.

pmc-12412380.title: The Necessity of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Training for Obstetrics and Gynecology: A Department-Wide Needs Assessment of an Academic Obstetrics and Gynecology Department
pmc-12412380.creator: Ayana GR DeGaia, Shilpa Darivemula, Omar M Young
pmc-12412380.description: Introduction:The persistent disparities in the field of obstetrics and gynecology (OBGYN) have become increasingly visible in the public eye, while at the same time public discourse regarding the appropriateness and efficacy of diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) education has become increasingly politically polarized.

pmc-12441308.title: Inhibition of Iron Death by Lycium barbarum Polysaccharides Ameliorates Myocardial Injury in Sepsis: A Pharmacological Mechanism Study Based on the NRF2/HO‐1 Pathway
pmc-12441308.creator: Zesu Niu, Yi Hu, Long Yang, Xiaorui Meng, Mengfei Chen, Xue Bai, Ruxin Liu, Yujiao Tang, Liting Yang, Weiliang Xue
pmc-12441308.description: Sepsis remains a leading global cause of mortality, with sepsis‐induced myocardial injury (SIMI) being a critical determinant of clinical outcomes. Lycium barbarum L. (goji berry), a traditional Chinese herb, has demonstrated therapeutic potential in sepsis‐related organ injuries through multiple pathways. However, its role and mechanisms in SIMI remain unexplored.

pmc-12731355.title: Helmet Therapy for Deformational Plagiocephaly: Clinical Outcomes and Considerations
pmc-12731355.creator: Sum-Yuet Ching, Oscar Chun-Yiu Wong, Wai-Wang Chau, Alec Lik-Hang Hung, Tsz-Ping Lam, Adam Yiu-Chung Lau
pmc-12731355.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Helmet therapy significantly reduces head deformity of infants with deformational plagiocephaly.Wearing the helmet for at least 6 h per day during sleep improves head shape.Low helmet compliance (0–5 h/day) results in no improvement or deterioration, whereas all patients with high compliance (≥18 h/day) demonstrate improvement. What is the implications of the main findings?

pmc-13075513.title: Severe Early-Onset Withdrawal Following Intentional Use of Mitragynine Pseudoindoxyl: A Case Report and Emerging Clinical Considerations
pmc-13075513.creator: Corneliu N Stanciu
pmc-13075513.description: Kratom is increasingly used in the United States for pain, mood, anxiety, and opioid substitution. Traditional kratom produces mild, delayed withdrawal, but semisynthetic derivatives such as mitragynine pseudoindoxyl (MP) are highly potent μ-opioid receptor agonists with δ-opioid receptor antagonism, leading to rapid-onset, full-spectrum opioid-like withdrawal.

pmc-13138409.title: Rheumatic Digital Twin: Proposed Machine Learning–Based Multimodal Framework to Inform Clinical Decision-Making
pmc-13138409.creator: Daniyal Selani, Rachel Knevel, Marcel Reinders, Erik B van den Akker, Andrew Coristine
pmc-13138409.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Rheumatic diseases are chronic, immune-mediated conditions characterized by significant heterogeneity in presentation and disease course. However, current clinical approaches often rely on snapshot-based assessments that fail to capture the complex longitudinal evolution of these conditions.

pmc-13226483.title: The dual-path association between upward social comparison and short video addiction: parallel mediating roles of negative emotions and psychological resilience
pmc-13226483.creator: Yuan Tian, Xianli Wang
pmc-13226483.description: BackgroundShort video addiction among college students has attracted increasing attention. Although upward social comparison has been linked to short video addiction, it remains unclear how negative emotions and psychological resilience jointly explain this association, and whether relevant pathways differ by gender.

pmc-13280582.title: Community Health Centres as a model of care: contextualizing for Europe – a Delphi study
pmc-13280582.creator: Antonija Poplas Susic, Diederik Aarendonk, Jan De Maeseneer, Toni Dedeu

pmc-13562716.title: The vicious cycle of SASP and inflammaging promotes aging and age-related diseases
pmc-13562716.creator: Qian Liu, Yulin Zheng, Chongkui Sun
pmc-13562716.description: Senescent cells accumulate in aging tissues and secrete a complex array of bioactive factors that alter the surrounding environment. While transient signaling can support tissue repair, persistent activity drives chronic low-grade inflammation and contributes to age-related diseases. These factors can spread damage to nearby cells and disrupt immune balance, creating a self-reinforcing cycle.

pmc-13700390.title: β-cell adaptation to increased insulin demand is a swift and dynamic process orchestrated by unfolded protein response
pmc-13700390.creator: Laura Maria Daian, Andrei Mircea Vacaru, Gabriela Tanko, Elena Mirela Lamba, Oana-Ana-Maria Mardare, Luiza Ghila, Simona Chera, Ana-Maria Vacaru
pmc-13700390.description: Pancreatic β-cells adapt to increased insulin demand through coordinated functional and molecular responses. However, in diabetes, these adaptive pathways eventually fail, driving β-cell dysfunction and demise. One of these pathways is unfolded protein response (UPR), a complex network of sensors and effectors that cooperate to restore endoplasmic reticulum (ER) function under stress.
